topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture by framing cancer development as an evolutionary process influenced by mutations, cell types, and microenvironmental factors.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic drivers of clonal selection
topics.groupedBecause: They describe how somatic mutations and transient epigenetic alterations confer competitive growth advantages that drive clonal expansion in tissue spaces.

topics.label: Cell of origin and cancer stem cell hierarchy
topics.groupedBecause: They investigate how tissue hierarchies, stem cell properties, and specific cells of origin influence tumor initiation and propagation.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and inflammatory promotion of tumor growth
topics.groupedBecause: They demonstrate how chronic inflammation, environmental stimuli, and supportive stroma cooperate with mutations to promote and sustain malignancy.

topics.label: Methodological approaches for investigating tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: It details the experimental models, sequencing technologies, and spatial omics used to analyze cellular plasticity and evolutionary dynamics in tumors.

topics.label: Integrated evolutionary model of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: It synthesizes the complex interactions among mutational events, cell-of-origin properties, transcriptional states, and microenvironmental conditions in driving cancer evolution.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: It closes the session and provides housekeeping by previewing the upcoming lecture on cancer therapy.
